claim: AWS provides the compute, storage and memory of an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory; you state your needs by choosing an edition (Standard, Enterprise or Hybrid), and you add domain controllers when you need more resources.
question: Can you configure the storage, CPU or memory of an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory?

values.display: AWS provides the compute, storage, and memory resources
add additional domain controllers to your directory

qualifiers.scope: per AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory

evidence.quote: As part of the fully managed service, AWS provides the compute, storage, and memory resources. As a customer, you declare your requirements when selecting your edition (Standard, Enterprise, or Hybrid), and AWS handles the infrastructure management. If you need more resources, you can add additional domain controllers to your directory.

note: Hybrid Edition is a recent edition; the numbers+changes lens should date it (examinable only if GA before 2026-07-15).

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD Standard and Enterprise editions accept schema extensions submitted as an LDIF file; you may extend but not modify the core Active Directory schema.
question: Does AWS Managed Microsoft AD support schema extensions, and can you change the core schema?

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Standard and Enterprise editions) supports schema extensions that you submit to the service in the form of a LDAP Data Interchange Format (LDIF) file. You may extend but not modify the core Active Directory schema.

claim: You add domain controllers to AWS Managed Microsoft AD through the Directory Service console or API; promoting EC2 instances to domain controllers manually is not supported.
question: Can you add domain controllers to AWS Managed Microsoft AD by promoting your own EC2 instances?

values.display: AWS Directory Service console or API

evidence.quote: You can add additional domain controllers to your managed domain using the AWS Directory Service console or API . Note that promoting Amazon EC2 instances to domain controllers manually is not supported.

claim: By default an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory is deployed across two Availability Zones in a Region and connected to your VPC.
question: How many Availability Zones does an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory use by default?

qualifiers.scope: per AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, per Region
qualifiers.condition: more domain controllers can be added

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD directories are deployed across two Availability Zones in a region by default and connected to your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD takes a backup automatically once per day, and its EBS volumes are encrypted at rest.
question: How often is AWS Managed Microsoft AD backed up, and is its data encrypted at rest?

qualifiers.scope: per AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory

evidence.quote: Backups are automatically taken once per day, and the Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes are encrypted to ensure that data is secured at rest.

claim: A failed AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain controller is replaced automatically in the same Availability Zone with the same IP address, and a full disaster recovery can use the latest backup.
question: What happens when an AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain controller fails?

values.display: automatically replaced in the same Availability Zone

evidence.quote: Domain controllers that fail are automatically replaced in the same Availability Zone using the same IP address, and a full disaster recovery can be performed using the latest backup.

claim: Every AWS Directory Service directory is deployed across multiple Availability Zones, monitoring detects and replaces failed domain controllers, and data replication and automated daily snapshots are configured for you.
question: What high-availability work does AWS Directory Service do for you?

evidence.quote: There is no need to build out your own complex, highly-available directory topology because each directory is deployed across multiple Availability Zones, and monitoring automatically detects and replaces domain controllers that fail. In addition, data replication and automated daily snapshots are configured for you.

claim: AWS Directory Service lets you assign IAM roles to users and groups in AWS Managed Microsoft AD, Simple AD, or an on-premises Active Directory through AD Connector, and gives a customer-specific console URL where they sign in with corporate credentials.
question: How does AWS Directory Service give directory users single sign-on to the AWS Management Console?

evidence.quote: AWS Directory Service allows you to assign IAM roles to AWS Manage Microsoft AD or Simple AD users and groups in the AWS cloud, as well as an existing, on-premises Microsoft Active Directory users and groups using AD Connector.
AWS Directory Service will provide a customer-specific URL for the AWS Management Console which users can use to sign in with their existing corporate credentials.

claim: Users in AWS Managed Microsoft AD can use Office 365: identities sync to Azure AD with Azure AD Connect, and AD FS with AWS Managed Microsoft AD authenticates the users.
question: Can users managed in AWS Managed Microsoft AD sign in to Office 365?

values.display: Microsoft Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS)

evidence.quote: You can synchronize identities from AWS Managed Microsoft AD to Azure AD using Azure AD Connect and use Microsoft Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) for Windows 2016 with AWS Managed Microsoft AD to authenticate Office 365 users.

note: The FAQ uses the old names Office 365 and Azure AD (now Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra ID).

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD supports LDAPS in both client and server roles; as a server it supports LDAPS over ports 636 (SSL) and 389 (TLS).
question: Can traffic between applications and AWS Managed Microsoft AD be encrypted with LDAPS, and on which ports?

values.display: in both client and server roles

qualifiers.condition: server-side LDAPS needs a certificate installed on the domain controllers

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD supports Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) over Secure Socket Layer (SSL) / Transport Layer Security (TLS), also known as LDAPS, in both client and server roles. When acting as a server, AWS Managed Microsoft AD supports LDAPS over ports 636 (SSL) and 389 (TLS).

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD Standard Edition includes 1 GB of directory object storage, which AWS estimates supports up to 5,000 users or 30,000 directory objects.
question: How many users and objects does AWS Managed Microsoft AD Standard Edition support?

qualifiers.condition: estimate; object sizes vary by company

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Standard Edition) includes 1 GB of directory object storage. This capacity can support up to 5,000 users or 30,000 directory objects, including users, groups, and computers.

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD Enterprise and Hybrid Editions include 17 GB of directory object storage, which AWS estimates supports up to 100,000 users or 500,000 objects.
question: How many users and objects do AWS Managed Microsoft AD Enterprise and Hybrid Editions support?

qualifiers.scope: per Enterprise or Hybrid Edition directory
qualifiers.condition: estimate; object sizes vary by company

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Enterprise and Hybrid Editions) includes 17 GB of directory object storage, which can support up to 100,000 users or 500,000 objects.

claim: Multi-Region replication of AWS Managed Microsoft AD is available in Enterprise Edition only, for new and existing directories.
question: Which AWS Managed Microsoft AD edition supports multi-Region replication?

evidence.quote: This feature is available in AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Enterprise Edition) only. You can use the feature for new and existing directories.

claim: With multi-Region replication, the directory keeps the same directory ID in the new Region and is deployed in the same AWS account as the primary Region.
question: Does a replicated AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory get a new directory ID or account in the added Region?

values.display: remains the same in the new region

evidence.quote: Your directory identifier (directory_id) remains the same in the new region and is deployed in the same AWS account as your primary Region.

claim: With multi-Region replication, directory sharing settings are not replicated from the primary Region automatically; you share the directory with other accounts per Region.
question: Are directory sharing settings copied to the other Regions of a replicated AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory?

values.display: not automatically replicated from the primary region

evidence.quote: Yes, with multi-region replication you have the flexibility to share your directory with other AWS accounts per Region. Directory sharing configurations are not automatically replicated from the primary region.

claim: You cannot remove the primary Region of a replicated AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory unless you delete the directory.
question: Can you remove the primary Region from a multi-Region AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory?

values.display: You cannot remove the primary Region

evidence.quote: You cannot remove the primary Region, unless you delete the directory.

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD does not allow direct host access to domain controllers through Remote Desktop, PowerShell Remoting, Telnet or SSH.
question: Can you log in to the domain controllers of AWS Managed Microsoft AD with RDP or SSH?

values.display: does not allow direct host access

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD does not allow direct host access to domain controllers via Windows Remote Desktop Connection, PowerShell Remoting, Telnet, or Secure Shell (SSH).

claim: When you create an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, you get an organizational unit (OU) and an administrative account with delegated administrative rights for that OU.
question: What administrative rights do you get in AWS Managed Microsoft AD?

values.display: delegated administrative rights for the OU

evidence.quote: When you create an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, you are assigned an organizational unit (OU) and an administrative account with delegated administrative rights for the OU.

claim: For Standard and Enterprise Editions, AWS provides no tools to migrate an existing Active Directory into AWS Managed Microsoft AD; you plan the migration yourself, including password resets.
question: Does AWS provide tools to migrate an on-premises Active Directory into AWS Managed Microsoft AD Standard or Enterprise?

values.display: does not provide any migration tools

evidence.quote: For Standard and Enterprise Editions, AWS does not provide any migration tools to migrate your existing Active Directory to AWS Managed Microsoft AD. You must establish a strategy for performing migration including password resets and implement the plans using Remote Server Administration Tools.

claim: With Hybrid Edition, you extend an existing Active Directory to AWS without a full migration: the AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain controllers join your existing forest and AD data replicates into AWS.
question: How does AWS Managed Microsoft AD Hybrid Edition differ from Standard and Enterprise for an existing Active Directory?

values.display: extend your existing Active Directory to AWS
become part of your existing AD forest

evidence.quote: For Hybrid Edition, you can extend your existing Active Directory to AWS without fully migrating. Your AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain controllers become part of your existing AD forest, and your AD data is replicated from your AD environments into AWS, creating a unified directory experience across environments.

note: Hybrid Edition is new; date its GA from the Directory Service document history before teaching it (not examinable if GA after 2026-07-15).

claim: Seamless domain join from the console works only at instance launch; existing EC2 Windows or Linux instances are joined with the EC2 API or PowerShell on the instance instead.
question: Can you use seamless domain join from the console for an EC2 instance that is already running?

values.display: You cannot use the seamless domain join feature

evidence.quote: You cannot use the seamless domain join feature from the AWS Management Console for existing EC2 for Windows Server and EC2 for Linux instances, but you can join existing instances to a domain using the EC2 API or by using PowerShell on the instance.

Seamless domain join is a feature that allows you to join your Amazon EC2 for Windows Server and Amazon EC2 for Linux instances seamlessly to a domain, at the time of launch and from the AWS Management Console.

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD Standard and Enterprise can be a resource forest of mainly computers and groups, with trust relationships to your directory on premises or in the cloud.
question: Can AWS Managed Microsoft AD act as a resource forest that trusts an on-premises directory?

evidence.quote: You can use AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Standard and Enterprise Editions) as a resource forest that contains primarily computers and groups with trust relationships to your directory hosted on-premises or on the cloud.

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD has the controls to help you meet HIPAA requirements and is in scope for PCI DSS.
question: Can AWS Managed Microsoft AD be used for workloads under HIPAA or PCI DSS?

values.display: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS)

evidence.quote: Yes. AWS Managed Microsoft AD has implemented the controls necessary to enable you to meet the U.S. Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) requirements and is included as an in-scope service in the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) Attestation of Compliance and Responsibility Summary.
